sentences.text:
Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer conducted a fresh enquiry, fixed the market value of the land in question @
Rs.7,000/- per acre and with all the benefits, determined the compensation payable at Rs.59,306/-.
3. Feeling dissatisfied with the said fixation, the appellant / claimant sought for reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and for enhancement @ Rs.1,30,000/- per acre.
4. Before the Reference Court, the appellant / claimant examined himself as P.W.1 and one Mr.P.Mallikarjuna Reddy as P.W.2 and got marked Exs.A1 and A2.
The Referring Officer was examined as R.W.1 and no documentary evidence was marked.

5. The learned Reference Court while considering the issue as to whether the appellant / claimant established his case for enhancement of the market value, enhanced the same from Rs.7,000/- per acre to Rs.11,200/- per acre.
6.

The learned counsel for the appellant / claimant inter alia contended that the learned Reference Court had failed to consider the matter in the proper perspective and erred in not awarding the compensation @ Rs.1,30,000/- per acre as claimed by the appellant.

He submits that the subject matter land was being irrigated under bore wells and crops like paddy, ground nut etc., were being raised and Rs.1,30,000/- per acre claimed by the appellant reflects the real market value of the land.

He submits that both the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the appellant supports the claim for enhancement, however the learned Reference Court despite the said evidence, was not justified in fixing the market value at a meager sum of Rs.11,200/- per acre.

He submits that it is a known fact that there will always be an upward trend of the market values of the land and in the light of the material on record, the learned Reference Court should have fixed the compensation @
Rs.1,30,000/- per acre, as sought for.
Making the said submissions, the learned counsel urges for allowing the appeal.
7. On the other hand, Mr.T.S.Rayalu, the learned Government Pleader for Appeals, made submissions to sustain the order under challenge.

It is his contention that the enhancement of compensation to the extent of Rs.11,200/- per acre by the Reference Court was based on cogent reasons and the appellant having failed to substantiate his claim, is not entitled for any relief in the present appeal.
He submits that there are no merits in the Appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.
8. Considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.
At the outset, it may be noted that Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act in respect of the subject matter land was issued on 02.01.1988.

At the time of Award Enquiry, 16 sale transactions which took place during the period of three years preceding the date of acquisition i.e., from 03.01.1985 to 02.01.1988 were taken into consideration for fixing the market value of the lands in question.

To disprove that the said fixation is not correct and to substantiate the claim for enhancement @

sentences.text: The version of P.W.2 that the market value was in fact Rs.40,000/- per acre, but for the purpose of registration it was reduced, was not appreciated by the learned Reference Court.
Except Ex.A1, the appellant did not adduce any evidence to substantiate the claim for Rs.1,30,000/- per acre.

That apart, the appellant / claimant had not placed any evidence with regard to the yield from the subject matter land by raising commercial crops and in fact in the cross examination, he admitted that no bore well is existing in the acquired land.
Be that as it may.

9. The learned Reference Court under the above circumstances, had taken into consideration the evidence of R.W.1, wherein, in cross- examination, he admitted that his predecessor in office, as Land Acquisition Officer after gathering the sale transactions, fixed the price @ Rs.11,000/- per acre for the acquired lands situated in Vallur and Kotlur villages and the Joint Collector, who inspected the lands, reduced the market value from Rs.11,000/- to Rs.7,000/- per acre.

The learned Reference Court, while recording that the Land Acquisition Officer had followed the method of arriving at the market value of the acquired land by gathering statistics of sale transactions preceding three years prior to the date of Notification of acquisition, was inclined to consider the market price @
Rs.11,000/- per acre as fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Such a view taken by the learned Reference Court in the absence of any material to substantiate the case of appellant for enhancement, cannot be found fault with.
The learned Reference Court had given cogent reasons for not enhancing the compensation as sought for by the appellant in toto and its appreciation of evidence on record was flawless.

Though the learned counsel for the appellant sought to impress upon the Court that the appellant is entitled for more compensation, in the absence of any supporting material, this Court has no alternative, except to confirm the order under appeal.
10. For the conclusions arrived at supra, the Appeal fails and accordingly the same is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, the Miscellaneous Applications pending, if any, shall also stand dismissed.
